text: In 2024, Toronto City Council directed Environment, Climate and Forestry to report back on current and future climate resilience initiatives across the corporation, provide a refreshed governance approach to climate resilience, identify climate resilience priorities and discuss Indigenous worldviews and relationships in climate resilience planning. This report responds to this direction, and has been prepared in coordination with two other heat-related reports being presented to City Council: Towards Implementing a Maximum Indoor Temperature Requirement for Rental Units and Cooling Rooms, led by Municipal Licensing and Standards Division (and co-signed by Toronto Public Health and Environment, Climate and Forestry), and Strengthening the Heat Relief Strategy, led by Toronto Emergency Management. Together, these reports contribute to a coordinated approach to enhancing heat resilience…

City Council on December 16 and 17, 2025, adopted the following: 1.
